extras.quota_verbatim: Open-budget microgrant: no fixed cap. Third-party trackers report a $1k-$50k typical range and up to $100k over two years, but the programme itself publishes no range - budgets are evaluated case by case. Rolling applications, one 1,500-word proposal, occasional 10-15 minute interview.
extras.limits_verbatim: Applicants must be at least 13 years old; one application per applicant per project. AI-written applications are now rejected outright ('We will test all submissions and reject those using AI for anything other than proofreading') - relevant given how this research was produced.
extras.chaining_verbatim: Dedicated tranches (Africa/Caribbean, India, UK Dynamism, Ukraine, Archaeology, Travel for Career Development, US Science Policy) each have their own budget, so a project can be aimed at the tranche where it fits best.
extras.agent_focus: Bulk data programmes that pay for your storage. Two halves: (1) institutional/gov repositories and cloud open-data sponsorships, judged as free byte pools; (2) research grants that could fund storage for an unaffiliated individual. Revisited AWS ODS, Google Cloud public datasets, Source Cooperative. Central question for each: what is the unit of quota (account / record / dataset / collection / project), because that unit is the multiplier.
